items.title: Delhi High Court quashes criminal defamation case against Senior Advocate Pinaki Misra

items.title: Trilegal Counsel Rajendra Dangwal goes independent
items.summary: Rajendra Dangwal is starting an independent practice as an arguing counsel specialising in commercial disputes as well as writ proceedings. Dangwal is a 2017 alumnus of National Law University, Jodhpur. He began his practice as a junior to Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain and specialised in constitutional law. He assisted and appeared alongside Hossain in several constitutional cases of national importance including the Right to Privacy case and the Aadhaar challenge. At Trilegal, Dangwal expanded into a commercial litigation profile and specialised in construction and infrastructure disputes, shareholder disputes, employment disputes and investigations, in addition to writ proceedings. As an independent practitioner, Dangwal will address the following practice areas: (i) corporate commercial and contractual disputes; (ii) construction, infrastructure and real estate; (iii) employment and service; (iv) sector specific regulatory disputes specifically telecom, insurance, and aviation sectors. items.title: Punjab & Haryana High Court flags non-cooperation of police witnesses in NDPS cases, summons top cop
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Tuesday summoned the Director General of Police (Law and Order) over repeated non-cooperation of official witnesses in the trials under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act [Naseeb Singh v State of Punjab] Justice Sumeet Goel observed that official witnesses in NDPS cases, who in most cases are police personnel, consistently fail to appear before the trial courts to tender their evidence, despite the issuance of bailable warrants and even non-bailable warrants. The Court added that there are several cases where even bailable warrants remain unexecuted for extended periods, resulting in routine adjournments of trials under the NDPS Act. "This state of affairs reflects a deeply disturbing and systemic lapse in the prosecutorial mechanism, whereby the trial is stalled indefinitely due to the indifference or willful non-cooperation of official witnesses. Such conduct not only frustrates the right of the accused—whether incarcerated or on bail—to a speedy trial as enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, but also gravely undermines the administration of criminal justice," the Court said. items.title: NLSIU cancels 2026 convocation after students oppose CJI's presence
items.summary: The National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, has cancelled its 34th Annual Convocation for the graduating batch of 2026, which was scheduled to be held on September 12, citing “unavoidable circumstances”. The decision comes weeks after students and alumni raised objections to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra attending the ceremony. NLSIU's Academic Administration team had informed graduating students on August 3 that September 12 was the proposed date for the annual convocation. However, a notice issued by the university on Thursday said the ceremony would no longer be held. “Despite our collective best efforts, due to unavoidable circumstances, we are unable to hold the 34th Annual Convocation,” the university said in its notice dated August 27. The university said all graduating students would instead be conferred their degrees in absentia, after due approvals from its governing bodies. Students will have the option of receiving their certificates by courier or collecting them from the campus. Earlier this year, the NCLT appointed a third member to decide the case after Judicial Member Ashok Kumar Bhardwaj and Technical Member Reena Sinha Puri delivered conflicting opinions on a repayment plan. While Bhardwaj favoured approval of the repayment plan, Puri concluded that it suffered from serious legal and procedural defects. items.title: Karnataka HC quashes criminal case against Coorg homestay owner booked for not reporting rape of US tourist
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed criminal proceedings against a Coorg homestay owner who was accused of failing to report the rape of US tourist who had stayed at the homestay [ Palecanda Ponappa v The State of Karnataka ]. Justice M Nagaprasanna observed that two of the charges levelled under against the homestay owner were the Foreigners Act, 1946. However, this law was repealed over seven months before the alleged offence took place. The Court, therefore, held that these charges cannot stand. " The incident forming the subject matter of the present proceedings is alleged to have occurred on 12-04-2026 i.e, more than seven months after the repeal had taken effect ... Criminality cannot be conjured out of a statutory provision which had ceased to exist when the alleged act occurred ," the Court said. Justice M Nagaprasanna The remaining charge was under Section 239 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which deals with the offence of intentionally failing to report crimes. items.title: US religious freedom panel seeks to revoke Mohan Bhagwat's visa
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) has expressed concern over Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat’s visit to the United States. It has urged the US government to consider targeted sanctions against RSS members and Indian officials allegedly linked to religious freedom violations. Bhagwat is currently visiting the US and is scheduled to speak at an event in New York City on Saturday, August 29. The report identified the RSS as the ideological parent of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). “We urge the US government to consider targeted sanctions against RSS members and Indian officials complicit in religious freedom violations, including revoking the visa issued to Mohan Bhagwat,” USCIRF Chair Asif Mahmood said in a statement on Wednesday, August 26. The RSS said in May that it had organised foreign visits to counter perceptions that it is a paramilitary organisation involved in attacks on minorities. items.title: Indian courts remain crucial for urgent relief despite rise of emergency arbitration: JSA Partner Dheeraj Nair
items.summary: Lawyers faced with an urgent threat to assets in India will still turn to courts despite the availability of emergency arbitration, JSA Partner Dheeraj Nair said on Thursday. Nair said that while emergency arbitration has gained recognition, an Indian court may still offer the quickest and most effective remedy when a party needs protection within a matter of days. “As a practitioner, the first thing that you will do is move to the Indian court, because you know that if it is a Friday evening also, perhaps by Monday morning, you will probably get the matter listed. But can an MCIA or SIAC give me an interim award or an interim order by Monday morning? I'm not so sure. So, practically speaking, we will still run to the court .” Nair was speaking at The Expanding Reach of Emergency Arbitration: A New Global Trend , a panel organised by the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA) and Drew & Napier as part of Singapore Convention Week 2026. The August 27 event in Singapore was part of a programme titled The India–Singapore Arbitration Corridor: Emergency Relief, Interim Measures & Cross-Border Challenges .
